report.summary: Chunk 3 of 3: implements analyse() and spectral_evidence() in daedalus/mapping/spectral.py
risks: spectral_evidence line 610 | medium | 'modules = ... or set(values)' may use values from fiedler even if partition is empty, but if values is also empty, modules becomes an empty set, returning empty dict; caller must handle missing modules gracefully. | Confirm intended fallback logic with fiedler values.
analyse line 575 | low | 'from . import reach' is inside function; if reach module fails to import, it raises ImportError at runtime. | Ensure reach module is always available or handle import error.

analyse line 589 | medium | 'scope' is set to list(scope_prefixes) or 'whole repo', but if scope_prefixes is empty list, it becomes empty list, not 'whole repo'. | Check if empty list should be treated as 'whole repo'.

handoff.purpose: Provides analyse() for computing four graph metrics and spectral_evidence() for flattening results per module.

symbols.name: analyse
symbols.note: May call reach.analyse(repo_root) which does a whole-repo pass (~11s), writes no files but reads filesystem. Otherwise no side effects.

symbols.name: spectral_evidence
symbols.note: Pure data transformation; no side effects.

claims.text: All four metrics over one graph.
claims.why: Function returns dict with keys fiedler, modularity, conductance, eigengap.

claims.text: Supply exactly one graph source: graph, report, or repo_root.
claims.why: Code checks graph, then report, then repo_root; returns error if none.

claims.text: reach.analyse is called -- a WHOLE-REPO PASS, MEASURED at ~11s on this tree, which is why no hot path calls this without being asked to.
claims.why: The 11s measurement is not in this chunk; reach.analyse is imported and called but its implementation is elsewhere.

claims.text: scope_prefixes is echoed into the result as scope so a reading can never be quoted without saying what it was taken over.
claims.why: Result dict has 'scope' key set to list(scope_prefixes) or 'whole repo'.

claims.text: See graph_from_reach for why you probably want ("daedalus/",).
claims.why: graph_from_reach is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Travels with every reading so a number can never be quoted without what it was measured over.

Carried so spectral_evidence can answer for EVERY module, including the disconnected ones -- islands are exactly the modules the picker asks about, and they are exactly the ones absent from the Fiedler scope. An enrichment that goes blank where it is needed is worse than none.
claims.why: Result includes 'partition' with all modules from partition, and spectral_evidence uses it to include all modules, even those not in fiedler values.

claims.text: The picker enriches an EXISTING candidate's evidence with these; it never creates a candidate from them and never lets them move a band.
claims.why: Picker logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A module that is not in the graph gets no row, so a caller that looks one up gets nothing rather than a zero that reads like a measurement.
claims.why: Code builds out dict only from modules in partition or fiedler values; missing modules are not added.

claims.text: spectral_fiedler_value is None for a module outside the Fiedler scope (an island, or any node off the largest component). None means NOT MEASURED -- never 0.0, which would read as "sits on the seam".
claims.why: values.get(module) returns None if module not in fiedler values; no default of 0.0.

observations.what: analyse() may call reach.analyse(repo_root) which is a heavy operation (~11s) and is only triggered when graph and report are None.
spectral_evidence() uses 'modules = ... or set(values)' which may fall back to values from fiedler if partition is empty or has no modules; if values is also empty, modules becomes empty set.

In analyse(), scope_prefixes is checked only when graph is not None; if graph is None, scope_prefixes is passed to graph_from_reach, but if graph is provided with scope_prefixes, an error is returned.
